page.overview:
What is The Simpsons (TV series)?

The Simpsons (often shortened to Simpsons) is an American long-running animated sitcom created by Matt Groening for the Fox Broadcasting Company. The main characters are a satire of a working-class family, consisting of Homer, Marge, Bart, Lisa, and Maggie. The series lampoons many aspects of American culture, society, politics, and history.

The cartoon made its debut as 60-second animated bumpers for The Tracey Ullman Show, with the first short airing on April 19, 1987. The shorts were then expanded into a full-length 30-minute television spin-off by Gracie Films and 20th Century Fox, first airing on December 17, 1989. As of 2025, 36 seasons have aired, and the 36th season ended on May 18, 2025, and Season 37 is currently airing as of September 28, 2025.

The series currently holds the record for the longest-running prime-time sitcom in the US, running for 35 years and 36 seasons, as well as three seasons of shorts since 1989, and has become the longest-running program on FOX.

The Simpsons was conceived in the lobby of James L. Brooks's office by Matt Groening. He was asked to do a series of animated shorts, and decided to do his Life in Hell series; since he realized that animating Life in Hell would require the rescinding of publication rights for his life's work, he chose another approach and formulated his version of a dysfunctional family. He named the characters after his own family and substituted Bart for his own name, as it was an anagram of 'brat'.
